messages:
Ada: heads-up: saw a regression in tail latency on a 4k-req workload when mmap-prefetch was enabled + aggressive host staging. not fully sure it's the prefetcher but metrics line up
Ben: can you paste the perf trace + the prefetch config that was used?
Ada: attaching snippet: ```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  lookahead_ms: 20
  window_packets: 8
  numa_affinity: prefer_local
  tl_prefetch_budget: 2048
```
Carla: interesting — 20ms lookahead seems high for small-batch interactive SLOs. prefetch will happily migrate pages into host staging which increases page churn and competes with the eviction stream.
Dmitri: are we seeing cross-tenant noisy-neighboring? last week's tenant demote changes reduced fairness, maybe side-effect.
Ada: tenant is a single heavy embedder run. CPU stalled on page fault streams, GPU queues backed up, then we hit our soft-SLO for 95p latency.
Ben: reminds me of the offload tradeoff we talked about: aggressive prefetch helps throughput for long-running batches but hurts P95 for short tails. We should expose an SLO-aware knob.
Carla: proposal: add a per-route prefetch_mode with enum {none, conservative, throughput} and a numerical "tail_sensitivity" [0..100] that biases policy. default conservative for hosted.
Dmitri: +1. but need to define what the knob actually changes: lookahead_ms, window_packets, and prefetch eviction priority. also whether prefetch touches pinned pages.
Ada: here's a concrete mapping idea: 
- none -> lookahead_ms=0, window_packets=0
- conservative -> lookahead_ms=5, window_packets=2, demoted_priority=low
- throughput -> lookahead_ms=50, window_packets=16, demoted_priority=high
Also tail_sensitivity can scale lookahead_ms linearly: lookahead_ms = base * (1 - tail_sensitivity/100)
Ben: that linear scaling seems too naive. tail tails are non-linear with page fault cost. Suggest piecewise: 0-30 -> base*0.5, 31-70 -> base*0.8, 71-100 -> base*1.2.
Carla: whatever we pick, we need to keep host staging compaction in the loop. otherwise prefetch will fragment host slab and make subsequent allocations worse. we should record a prefetch fingerprint in slab telemetry to help compaction target hotspots.
Dmitri: telemetry note: emit prefetch_id + route + tenant + affected_pages_count in offload telemetry event. infra-bot: logged: PREFETCH_EVENT schema accepted.
Ada: another surface: for Dedicated and Private, customers may want to opt into kernel-level madvise(WILLNEED) vs our user-space thrash-controlled prefetch. need compatibility layer in mmap shim.
Ben: API boundary idea: allocator->offload-agent handshake with signals: PREPARE_PREFETCH(route, budget, hint_id) and PREFETCH_COMPLETE(hint_id, stats) so the serving runtime can make rollback decisions.
Carla: sketch of handshake in pseudo: ```c
int prepare_prefetch(route_id, budget_tokens) {
  hint = alloc_hint();
  hint->budget = budget_tokens;
  agent_queue_push(PREPARE_PREFETCH, hint);
  return hint->id;
}
void on_prefetch_complete(int hint_id, stats) {
  // fallback logic: if stats.faults > threshold, reduce lookahead for route
}
```
Dmitri: fallback logic should tie into rollout/console: automatic soft-fallback for routes exceeding a tail-fault-rate for 10m window. + audit logs.
Ada: I also ran a small experiment: disabling prefetch reduced P95 by ~18% but increased total tokens/sec by 7% under long-run embed workloads. so users will trade either direction.
Ben: action items:
- define route-level prefetch_mode + tail_sensitivity API (Carla)
- implement PREFETCH_EVENT telemetry and prefetch_id propagation (Dmitri)
- add allocator <-> offload-agent handshake prototype (Ben)
- add canary in hosted with conservative default (Ada)
Carla: one more: ensure private deploys can toggle madvise-mode; add doc note for customer's ops teams about kernel prefetch caveats.
Ada: thanks. I'll open a short RFC with config schema + experiment logs. pinging @Dmitri and @Ben for review. :thumbsup:
Dmitri: will review tomorrow morning.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for eng-runtime/staging at 2026-03-24T02:00Z
Ben: ack, thanks infra-bot.
Carla: quick Q — should this change interact with KV cache warming? prefetch duplicates if we warm the same prefixes. we should dedupe based on prefix fingerprint.
Ada: good point. add dedupe to action items.
Ben: final: let's keep defaults conservative to avoid wide regressions in hosted users.
Ada: agreed. I'll include recommended defaults and experiment data in RFC.
